deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from this folder and the previous page): Σ is an arrangement ('système') of pseudo-lines in the projective plane. A 'position relative' (p.r.) is the combinatorial position of an additional pseudo-line D with respect to Σ. In modern terms this is a one-element extension of the rank-3 oriented matroid of Σ. A position is 'critique' when D passes through vertices ('sommets') of Σ, i.e. it is a non-generic extension. The previous page found that the stable generalizations of a non-principal D through ν multiple vertices form the vertices of a ν-cube: 2^ν vertices and ν·2^(ν−1) edges. That is the local cell structure of the space of positions.

This page classifies 'balayages élémentaires', the elementary sweeps between two relative positions 1 and 2 of D.
- The two positions (brown curves) coincide outside a vertical strip (dashed lines).
- Inside the strip, the swept region contains no vertices of Σ other than marked ones a, b, c, ...
- Inside the strip, the only traces of lines of Σ are the marked pencils through those vertices.
- The green line is an intermediate generic position, between 1 and 2 in the drawings.

The cases:
- (I_1): one vertex a. Position 2 bumps over a and passes through it; position 1 passes beside it. The sweep is asymmetric: position 1 is not critical (at least not because of this region).
- (I_2): two vertices. Position 2 goes through a, position 1 through b. a and b are joined by a segment of a line of Σ (arrows a↔b). The intermediate position crosses that segment. Symmetric: 1 is critical iff 2 is.
- (I_3): a and b on position 2, c on position 1, joined by a zigzag c→a, c→b along lines of Σ. Asymmetric (2 vertices vs 1), yet 1 is critical iff 2 is.
- General (I_n), drawn for n=7 (4 vertices above, 3 below): a sweep from one critical position to another across a zigzag of n vertices alternating between the two positions. It is asymmetric exactly when n is odd.

The point of the dichotomy: n=1 is the only case where one end can fail to be critical. For n≥2 both ends carry at least one vertex of the region, so criticality is equivalent. The sweeps I_n with n≥2 are thus moves between critical positions, i.e. 'edges' connecting the cells of the space of positions. The next page continues with pictures of the same type.

Purpose: describe the adjacency/connectivity structure of the set of relative positions of a pseudo-line with respect to Σ, in modern terms the extension space of a rank-3 oriented matroid, via local elementary moves.
errors: No mathematical error visible. Ambiguities: 'critique' is not defined on this page, so the claim 'n=1 asymmetric, position 1 not critical' only makes sense locally (position 1 may still be critical through vertices outside the strip). Read literally, 'critical iff' for n≥2 needs that same local reading.
The role of the green line (intermediate generic position vs. a reference pseudo-line) is not stated. It is not a line of Σ, since the text says the only traces of Σ are the marked ones.

ideas.what: Relative positions of an extra pseudo-line with respect to an arrangement Σ; critical positions through vertices of Σ
ideas.modern_name: One-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid / extension space (Las Vergnas lattice of extensions)

ideas.what: Elementary sweeps I_n: D moved across a region containing only n vertices arranged in a zigzag along lines of Σ, alternating between the two end positions
ideas.modern_name: Local moves/flips between adjacent cells of the extension space; generalized (multiple) Ringel flips of Σ∪{D}; sweeping a pseudoline across vertices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ringel (1956, flips); Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences); Edelsbrunner–Guibas / Snoeyink–Hershberger (topological sweeps, 1986–89)

ideas.what: Parity dichotomy: I_n symmetric iff n even; n=1 the only case where one end is non-critical; for n≥2, position 1 critical iff position 2 critical
ideas.modern_name: Elementary combinatorial observation on the extension space

missed.claim: A classification of elementary sweeps (I_n) as the basic adjacencies between critical relative positions. Together with the previous page's ν-cube of stable generalizations, this amounts to a hands-on cell structure for the space of one-element extensions of a pseudoline arrangement, about a decade before Sturmfels–Ziegler's study of extension spaces. Whether Grothendieck derived connectivity or topology results from it is not visible on this page.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical. It documents Grothendieck independently working on the combinatorial topology of extension spaces of rank-3 oriented matroids, a topic linked to the extension space conjecture and later counterexamples in high rank. No new theorem is evident here.

deep.surprise_reason: Careful, original-looking combinatorics of the extension space of pseudoline arrangements, predating the main literature. The content of this page itself (a list of local sweep types with a parity remark) is elementary.
transcription_corrections: Bottom caption likely reads 'balayage [-élémentaire-] de p.r. critique à une autre', not 'à une sortie [?]'.
In (I_1): 'la position 1 n'est pas [-jamais-] p.r. critique'; the comma after '1' is spurious.
Opening title: 'balayages élémentaires des positions relatives' (correct). The words 'asymétrique'/'symétrique' are underlined in the original, not struck out.

In (I_2) the label at the top vertex is 'a' written over a struck letter. Bold arrows run between b and a in (I_2) and from c to a and from c to b in (I_3); they mark segments of lines of Σ joining the vertices.
